question: The practice of sati was made illegal and punishable in the year 1829, under Governor-General ______________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The practice of sati was made illegal and punishable in the year 1829.
 
• This legislation was enacted under the authority of Governor-General William Bentinck.
 
• Sati was the practice where a widow would immolate herself on her husband's funeral pyre.
 
• The law was a significant social reform in British India and faced both support and resistance.
 
• This move was part of broader efforts to reform and modernize Indian society during the British colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**

 
 
• He was a prominent social reformer who actively campaigned against the practice of sati.
 
• His efforts were instrumental in the eventual abolition of sati.
 
 
 
• **Hindu Widow Remarriage Act**
 
 
• This Act was passed in 1856 to legalize the remarriage of Hindu widows.
 
• It was another significant step towards improving the social status of women in India.
 
 
 
• **William Bentinck's Reforms**
 
 
• Besides abolishing sati, Bentinck also took steps towards education reform and the suppression of the thuggee cult.
 
• His tenure is noted for several progressive social reforms in India.
